A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ViPRA and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H. Renumbered and relocated content can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and physical-robot experiments, including SIMPLER, LIBERO-10, and bimanual results in Appendix H.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds data-composition and optical-flow-loss ablation results in Tables 3–4.

M1.justification: The latent-action architecture, joint video/action pretraining, and chunked flow-matching controller remain unchanged. The explicit action encoder in Figure 2 and revised teacher-forcing pseudocode clarify components and procedures already described in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds an offline action-prediction probe targeting BridgeV2 actions. v1 documents BridgeV2 as an actionless pretraining source but reports no corresponding probe. The training corpora and SIMPLER, LIBERO-10, single-arm, and bimanual manipulation coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The LIBERO comparison changes from v1 Table 6 to v2 Table 8: UVA is added, UniVLA (human) is removed, and UniVLA (all) is retained as UniVLA with the same 0.92 score. UVA previously appeared only in the inference-speed comparison. Other comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: The new ablations introduce human-only and robot-only training controls, removal of optical-flow supervision, and a frozen-backbone action probe. Action MSE, perplexity, and entropy are added as diagnostic metrics. Existing benchmark protocols and documented training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5.5 adds focused tests of human-versus-robot data composition and optical-flow supervision, supported by Tables 3–4. Existing component ablations, latent-transfer examples, smoothness analyses, generalization observations, and bimanual case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 retains 10 runs with five random seeds per LIBERO task, totaling 500 episodes. The added ablations introduce no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Perplexity and entropy are diagnostic metrics, not new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: New ablation results include LIBERO success of 0.79/0.72/0.69 for combined/robot-only/human-only training and action MSE of 0.84 versus 0.92 with versus without flow supervision. LIBERO adds UVA at 0.90 and removes UniVLA (human) at 0.79. Main ViPRA scores remain unchanged. Section 5.4 changes π0's real-world average from 41.8% to 40.1%, although Figure 3 still shows 41.8%.

T1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises optical-flow summation bounds to avoid referencing frame L+1 outside the supplied 0–L clip. Algorithm 2 corrects the latent-chunk dimensionality. These are limited formal corrections; the rewritten LPIPS sum also introduces a mismatched summation index. No new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same central claims: motion-centric latent learning, joint future-state/action prediction, data-efficient continuous control up to 22 Hz, and headline gains of 16% in SIMPLER and 13% in real-world tasks.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new ablations as evidence that human videos supply motion diversity, robot videos ground dynamics, and flow supervision favors motion information. Section 6 replaces the brief tabletop limitation discussion with more specific concerns about dexterity, data diversity, and unknown scaling behavior.

D1.justification: v1 promises future resource release; v2 reports released code, models, latent-action-labeled data, and benchmark scripts, with a new Reproducibility section. SIMPLER finetuning-data release remains prospective. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time tables are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds NovaFlow, Patel et al.'s generated-video imitation work, and Video Generators are Robot Policies. The future-work discussion adds alignment and VLM-value references. These extend the literature coverage without substantially changing ViPRA's positioning; publication updates and citation-style changes are largely editorial.

P1.justification: v2 revises method explanations, result paragraphs, notation, and algorithm descriptions. It retitles Section 6 as Limitations and Future Work, organizes its discussion into topics, and adds Section 7 on reproducibility. The overall narrative and appendix organization remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v2 adds two ablation tables, updates labels and components in Figures 2 and 7, and relocates and renumbers the heatmaps, transfer examples, and smoothness plots. It adopts the ICLR template and revised author/header layout while retaining most visual content.

improvement.justification: Tables 3–4 add useful evidence about two previously untested design choices, and the expanded limitations and resource-release documentation improve transparency. The gains are limited by sparse probe-protocol details, unchanged uncertainty reporting, and the new π0 text–figure discrepancy. The core method and principal benchmark results remain stable.
